scenes.title: Dastillon [boxeur]
scenes.description: A press photograph from 1911 by Agence Rol shows the boxer Dastillon. It is held by the Bibliothèque nationale de France, département Estampes et photographie, and is in the public domain.
scenes.explanation: Smartwatches with illuminated digital displays did not exist in 1911, making this wrist device impossible for the era.

source.description: Référence bibliographique : Rol, 17351 Appartient à l’ensemble documentaire : Pho20Rol

scenes.title: Fête des Fleurs, [Paris, automobile fleurie]
scenes.description: A press photograph by Agence Rol showing a flower-decorated automobile at the Fête des Fleurs in Paris in 1908. The negative on glass is held by the Bibliothèque nationale de France, département Estampes et photographie, and the photograph appeared in La Vie illustrée in 1908.
scenes.explanation: Bright red LED bicycle tail lights did not exist in 1908; early bicycle lamps were carbide or oil, not battery-powered LEDs.

scenes.title: [Second projet de baldaquin soutenu par quatre paires de colonnes et orné d'un suspensoir]
scenes.description: A 1705 drawing in brown ink and wash by Robert de Cotte, titled "Second project of a baldachin supported by four pairs of columns and adorned with a suspensoir," shows an elevation of a baldachin design for the decoration of various unidentified altars. It is held by the Bibliothèque nationale de France, département Estampes et photographie, and is in the public domain.
scenes.explanation: The first practical visible-spectrum LED was only demonstrated in 1962, so a glowing LED candle cannot exist in a 1705 drawing.

scenes.title: [NF.WF 13607 Bragernes torg]
scenes.description: A photograph from 1940 in the collection of the National Library of Norway, catalogued as NF.WF 13607 Bragernes torg, showing Bragernes square. The record does not name a photographer.
scenes.anomaly: modern cargo bicycle with a boxy child seat
scenes.explanation: Molded plastic child seats for bicycles did not exist in 1940, so this accessory cannot belong to the scene.
scenes.credit: Wilse, Anders Beer, Norsk folkemuseum via National Library of Norway

scenes.description: [Blomsterhandel på torg] · National Library of Norway.
scenes.explanation: Molded plastic flower pots did not exist in 1890, when plant containers were made of wood, wicker, terracotta or metal.
